title: Exhausting the ball by concentric balls for a nonnegative continuous integrand
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, R > 0, E ∈ ℝ, and B := B̆_R(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n). Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous on B with f ≥ 0 on B. If ∫_{B̆_r(0)} f ≤ E for every r with 0 < r < R, then f is integrable on B and ∫_B f ≤ E.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R E : ℝ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ), 0 < R → ContinuousOn f (ball (0 : Euclid n) R) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Euclid n) R, 0 ≤ f x) → (∀ r, 0 < r → r < R → ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) r, f x ≤ E) → IntegrableOn f (ball (0 : Euclid n) R) ∧ ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid n) R, f x ≤ E
